text:
alex: seeing a short spike of apiserver 5xxs in eu-west1 starting ~1799996600, controller-manager restarted twice, leader election churning. graphs show watch retransmits up 10x.
smita: ugh, any correlation with GPU pool ops?
ajay: (jay) yes we had a bursty onboard of new GPU nodes from an internal test job, looked like ~2200 new pods in 90s.
alex: logs: `I0321 12:17:xx.123] apiserver: watch failed: net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout)` repeated.
miguel: conntrack high? NAT SNAT pools often the scapegoat for wide fanout during attach.
kai: `kubectl get --raw /metrics | grep watch` shows huge watcher counts.
jay: quick check: `conntrack -L | wc -l` -> 128900 ; sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 131072. basically saturated.
smita: that explains closed connections -> apiserver clients drop and controller-manager interprets as API uncertainty -> restarts.
alex: incident-bot? can we create an incident and mark mitigation?
oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260321-EU1 created by alex for apiserver 503s (priority: P1).
miguel: short-term mitigations: 1) throttle gpu-provisioner concurrency 2) bump conntrack limit on nodes + NAT gateways 3) add SNAT pool / ephemeral ip allocation to spread egress.
kai: adding to that: enable local pod SNAT on GPU nodes to keep track entries local? Might be tricky.
jay: I can flip a canary: scale gpu-provisioner down from 50->10 to stop new onboards; will do now.
smita: do we have a safe conntrack bump? ops note: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` but need to roll via image or daemonset for persistence.
alex: let's land hotfix: backoff provisioner + bump conntrack on a sample of nodes + add extra NAT egress for eu-west1. who owns NAT config?
miguel: infra owns it, i'll request extra egress IPs from cloud account, can be live within 8-12m.
jay: provisioner scaled -> stopped new onboards, watcher backlog is decreasing. apiserver 5xxs dropping.
kai: controller-manager restarts fewer now, leader election stabilized.
smita: action items: miguel request egress IPs; infra to prepare daemonset to bump conntrack safely; platform to add rate-limit to GPU provisioner next week.
alex: also cost note — adding NAT IPs will increase billed egress NAT/idle IP costs; flagging to finance for FYI.
miguel: noted. putting a runbook addendum: "If GPU bulk onboards happen, throttle provisioner + check conntrack and NAT pools".
jay: suggested follow-up: test scaling behaviour with synthetic onboarding in staging and validate conntrack headroom.
oncall-bot: INC-20260321-EU1 updated: mitigations applied (provisioner scaled, conntrack sample bumped), monitoring set.
alex: thanks team. leaving incident open until 24h stable and follow-ups completed. :thumbsup:
